finding.claim: /checkout trusts client-supplied price and qty when computing the charge amount. An attacker can set price to 0 or a tiny value, or use a negative qty or price, to pay little or nothing, or to produce a negative total (a refund or credit if the payment backend accepts it).
finding.sink: req.payments.charge(req.user.id, total) at cart.js:6, and the response at cart.js:7

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty, using values taken straight from the request body
charge is called with the attacker-derived total

finding.guards_checked: No server-side catalog price lookup. No validation of qty (integer, >= 1) or price (non-negative). No check that items are present or that the total is positive. The safer /checkout-v2 route exists but this legacy route is still mounted, so it is not mitigated. Auth middleware for req.user is not visible in this file.

verdict.guard_found: none in this file. The only auth-like reference is req.user.id, which is set by middleware that is not visible. /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10-18) has the fix (catalog price lookup, qty clamp) but /checkout does not use it.
verdict.reason: cart.js:5 sums request-supplied i.price * i.qty with no validation or catalog lookup, and cart.js:6-7 charge and return that total; the attacker only needs to be any authenticated customer, which is the intended user of checkout.

verdict_facts.reason: cart.js:5 computes total from client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no validation or catalog lookup, and cart.js:6 charges it; any authenticated user (req.user is set upstream) can reach the route, and only the separate /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10-18) does server-side pricing.
